supporting_authorities.description: Judicial review provision — federal district court jurisdiction to review final SSA decisions; substantial evidence standard
Disability definition for DIB purposes; disability freeze provisions
Basic definition of disability — regulatory implementation of § 423(d)

key_cases.holding: Supreme Court: substantial evidence standard applies to SSA disability determinations under § 405(g); hearsay medical reports may constitute substantial evidence
Due process minimum for disability benefit termination established; three-factor balancing test for procedural requirements

key_cases.citation: Cleveland v. Policy Mgmt. Sys. Corp., 526 U.S. 795 (1999)
key_cases.holding: SSDI claim for inability to work not judicially estopped from ADA claim; different definitional frameworks

legislative_history.origin: Social Security Amendments of 1956 (Pub. L. 84-880) — initial disability insurance program
legislative_history.disability_definition_added: Social Security Amendments of 1967 (Pub. L. 90-248) — tightened definition; added 'any other work in national economy' language at § 423(d)(2)(A)
legislative_history.note: Prior to 1967, disability could be established under a more permissive standard; the 1967 narrowing created the definition that still governs today
